look_here_first: Start at the base: this is a taprooted ANNUAL, not a rhizomatous perennial. Check flat, herbaceous, non-overlapping leaves; then inspect a mature cypsela with a loupe. The pappus is a minute thickened ring rather than the ~25 obvious bristles of C. ericoides. Compare whole plants with C. effusa and confirm root type before naming.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Small taprooted annual with slender, often branched, hairy stems; do not infer identity from overall height.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Basal and stem leaves alternate, flat and herbaceous rather than densely overlapping and leathery; basal leaves often wither by flowering.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Small solitary terminal radiate heads; pale rays around yellow disk florets; head color alone cannot distinguish the genus.

key_traits.label: Fruits
key_traits.text: Mature cypsela pappus reduced to a minute thickened ring (Flora of North America key); use magnification to avoid mistaking it for an absent pappus.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: Examine rootstock and annual/perennial habit; Examine basal and stem leaves including overlap and blade bases; Examine mature cypsela pappus with magnification

lookalikes.differences: C. effusa is a rhizomatous perennial with broad proximal cauline leaves 6–12 mm and a tiny ring-like pappus; C. ericoides is perennial with densely overlapping narrow leathery leaves and ~24–26 pappus bristles. Other annual Chaetopappa may have cups or bristle+scale pappi; check ripe fruits.
